The vaccine rollout was a mess. Appointments crashed online systems. Phone lines rang for hours with no answer. Eligible residents drove to neighboring counties -- sometimes neighboring states -- to find open slots. Rural clinics received a fraction of the doses they requested. Urban hospitals got more than they could administer before expiration. Coordination failed at every level. Federal agencies blamed state agencies. State agencies blamed local officials. Local officials blamed the software. Meanwhile, people waited. The elderly waited. The immunocompromised waited. Essential workers waited. Six months in, the numbers told the story plainly. Wealthy zip codes had double the vaccination rates of poor ones. The divide was predictable. It was also preventable. Logistics is not a mystery. Supply chains can be managed. Distribution can be equitable -- if equity is treated as a priority rather than an afterthought. It was not. The results speak for themselves.
